title: Duck typing, protocols and type hints
summary: If it quacks like a duck, and how to say so in types.

steps.title: Duck typing
body: In C# a method can accept an object only if its type implements the right interface. Python asks a different question: **does it have the method I am about to call?**
return sum(len(t) for t in things)
total_length(["ab", [1, 2, 3], {"k": 1}])   # 6: str, list, dict all have __len__

No declared interface is needed. That is **duck typing**: "if it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it is a duck". The `Notifier` you wrote in the last lesson worked with *any* object that had `send`.

steps.prompt: A function calls `for line in source:`. Which can you pass as `source`?
options: Anything iterable: a list, a file, a generator, your own class with `__iter__`
steps.explain: Duck typing: the `for` loop only needs `__iter__`. Nothing has to inherit from anything.

steps.title: Type hints
body: Type hints document types and let tools (mypy, pyright, your editor) check them. **Python itself ignores them at runtime.**
def greet(name: str, times: int = 1) -> str:
maybe: int | None = None          # C#: int?
`greet(42)` still runs; only a type checker complains. Think of hints as C#'s compile-time checking, made optional and run as a separate tool (module 8).

steps.explain: Hints are not enforced: `double("ab")` happily returns `abab`. They are stored in `__annotations__` for tools to read.

steps.title: Protocols: interfaces for duck typing
body: `typing.Protocol` describes the shape you need **without** requiring inheritance. It is a structural interface: any class with matching methods fits.
def broadcast(senders: list[Sender], msg: str) -> None:
A type checker accepts any object with a `send(str)` method. Add `@runtime_checkable` to also allow `isinstance(x, Sender)` checks at runtime.

steps.prompt: Match each hint to its meaning.
True at runtime in plain Python?
items: passing the wrong type raises `TypeError` automatically
a class can satisfy a `Protocol` without inheriting from it
you must declare types on every variable

steps.title: Sized things
prompt: Write a `runtime_checkable` `Protocol` called `HasArea` with a method `area(self) -> float`.
Then write `total_area(items: list[object]) -> float` that adds up `area()` for every item that matches `HasArea` (check with `isinstance`) and **ignores** the rest. Use type hints throughout.
solution: return sum(item.area() for item in items if isinstance(item, HasArea))
template: Dojo.check("a class with area() matches HasArea", isinstance(Sq(1), HasArea), "use @runtime_checkable and Protocol")
Dojo.check("a class without it does not", not isinstance(Blob(), HasArea), "")
Dojo.eq("ignores things without area", 4, total_area([Sq(2), Blob(), "text", 5]))
Dojo.check("total_area has a return hint", "return" in total_area.__annotations__, "add -> float")
hints: `sum(i.area() for i in items if isinstance(i, HasArea))`
